name: forest north-edge skyline of treetops (bamboo)
label: jp_city/jp-forest-bb-sky-0
reasons: 화풍: 칸 정보량이 기준보다 훨씬 낮음 (4/4)

surfaces.part: treetop canopy skyline (lit upper crown band with ragged silhouette)
dense foliage mass below the crown

answer.evidence: The piece is a tileable strip of foliage. Rows 11-17 form a ragged, lit crown silhouette that widens from 2 to 24 px and reaches the full 32 px at row 18. Rows 18-47 are a uniform dark-green foliage mass with leaf-cluster texture. There is no front-edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse, and no visible contents. The light highlights in rows 12-20 are only the lit upper edge of the foliage, not a separate horizontal surface. The object reads as a flat front-facing foliage wall with a skyline, so it has no true top surface. The column scan shows no edge line, only gradual dark-to-light texture variation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small bamboo treetop skyline block with only 9 distinct colours in total and a median of 9 per 16x16 tile. The references have a median of 108-109 per tile and 427-567 colours overall, so it is about an order of magnitude lower. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, and the dark edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so the outline is a dark green material tone rather than a black sticker line. There is some leaf-clump dotting in about 4 green steps, but the references use 6 or more with per-clump highlights and varied clusters. The silhouette is a plain rectangular block with a lumpy top edge. It lacks the layered clump highlights, depth and edge variation of the references. Even allowing for a simple skyline tile, it reads as thinner and flatter than the Beodeul standard.
